decisions.choice: This verse is 2:1 in the Hebrew text, 1:18 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text begins chapter 2 with the second vision, so that chapter 1 holds only the first. Many Bibles end chapter 1 with this vision, numbering 2:1-4 as 1:18-21, and then begin their chapter 2 with the man with the measuring line (Hebrew 2:5), so their 2:1-13 is 2:5-17 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates, and Zechariah is cited by the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: the second vision: four horns, and four craftsmen who throw them down
decisions.reason: A horn is the strength of an animal, and in the Bible it stands for power, especially the power of kings and nations (Psalm 75:5-6, 11; 1 Kings 22:11; Daniel 8:20-22). The angel explains that the horns are the powers that scattered God's people (verse 2), and the craftsmen are sent to throw them down (verse 4). The angel does not name the nations. Four is the number of the four directions (2:10; 6:5), so the horns may stand for every power, from every side, that had attacked Judah.

decisions.choice: I lifted up my eyes and saw: I looked up and saw something new
decisions.reason: The phrase marks the start of a new scene in a vision (2:5; 5:1; 6:1), as it does in stories (Genesis 18:2; 22:13).

decisions.choice: I looked up (B, R); look (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "looked up" for the idiom, and leave out "look", which only points to what was seen. The horns keep their name at every level, as set for Zechariah's visions.

decisions.choice: "alcé mis ojos ... y he aquí" (L), "alcé la vista" (B), "levanté la vista" (R); "cuernos"
decisions.reason: The idiom of a new scene (m3) is kept word for word at Literal and given as "looking up" at the other levels; the horns keep their name at every level.

decisions.choice: the vision narrated in the passé simple at L and B ("je levai", "je vis") and the passé composé at R ("j'ai levé", "j'ai vu")
decisions.reason: Zechariah's night visions are first-person narrative, as set for French in these books; the speech inside them stays in the present, future and passé composé.

vi.L: Tôi nói với thiên sứ đang nói với tôi: "Những [cái] này là gì?" Và người bảo tôi: "Đây [là] những cái sừng đã làm tan lạc Giu-đa, Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giê-ru-sa-lem."
vi.B: Tôi hỏi thiên sứ đang nói với tôi những cái sừng ấy là gì. Thiên sứ đáp: "Đây là những cái sừng đã làm tan lạc Giu-đa, Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giê-ru-sa-lem."
vi.R: Tôi hỏi thiên sứ đang nói với tôi những cái sừng ấy là gì. Thiên sứ bảo tôi: "Đó là những cái sừng đã làm cho Giu-đa, Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giê-ru-sa-lem bị tan lạc."

ko.L: 그래서 내가 나와 말하던 천사에게 말하였다. "이것들이 무엇입니까?" 그러자 그가 나에게 말하였다. "이것들은 유다와 이스라엘과 예루살렘을 흩어 버린 뿔들이다."
ko.B: 내가 나와 말하던 천사에게 그것들이 무엇인지 물었다. 그가 대답했다. "이것들은 유다와 이스라엘과 예루살렘을 흩어 버린 뿔들이다."
ko.R: 나는 나와 말하던 천사에게 그것들이 무엇인지 물었다. 그가 말해 주었다. "이것들은 유다와 이스라엘과 예루살렘을 흩어 버린 뿔들이다."

decisions.choice: scattered: drove the people into exile
decisions.reason: The verb is used for winnowing grain, tossing it so that the wind carries off the chaff (Isaiah 30:24), and for the scattering of the people among the nations (Jeremiah 31:10; Ezekiel 5:10). The horns are the powers that sent God's people into exile.

decisions.choice: Judah, Israel and Jerusalem: the whole people of God
alternatives: Israel as the northern kingdom, scattered by Assyria
decisions.reason: Israel may be the northern kingdom, which Assyria took into exile (2 Kings 17:6), named beside Judah and its capital, which Babylon destroyed. It may also be the name of the whole people. Either way, the three names cover all of God's people who were scattered. Verse 4 names Judah alone.

decisions.choice: These are the horns ... (every level)
decisions.reason: As set for Zechariah's visions, the angel's explanation is translated as he gives it, and no level adds who the horns are.

decisions.choice: "Hizi ni nini?"; "pembe" (class 10)
decisions.reason: The question takes the class of the things asked about: horns are things, so "hizi", where 1:9 asked about the horsemen with "hawa".

decisions.choice: craftsmen: skilled workers in wood, stone or metal
decisions.reason: The word is used for craftsmen of every kind (Exodus 35:35; Isaiah 44:12-13). Here they are probably workers with tools of iron, smiths who could cut or break off horns, though the text does not say what kind.

decisions.choice: the LORD himself showed me
decisions.reason: In most of the visions Zechariah simply sees, or the angel shows him. Here the LORD is the one who shows him, as he does in 3:1 (and compare Amos 7:1, 4, 7). The vision comes from God, not from Zechariah's own mind.

decisions.choice: skilled workers (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "skilled workers", a common phrase for people who work with their hands at a trade. The image is kept.

decisions.choice: "장인" (L, B), "솜씨 좋은 기술자" (R)
decisions.reason: The word covers craftsmen of every kind (m1), so Korean uses the general 장인 rather than naming smiths; Readable uses a plainer word, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֕ר מָ֛ה אֵ֥לֶּה בָאִ֖ים לַֽעֲשׂ֑וֹת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאמֹ֗ר אֵ֣לֶּה הַקְּרָנ֞וֹת אֲשֶׁר־זֵ֣רוּ אֶת־יְהוּדָ֗ה כְּפִי־אִישׁ֙ לֹא־נָשָׂ֣א רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ אֵ֨לֶּה֙ לְהַחֲרִ֣יד אֹתָ֔ם לְיַדּ֞וֹת אֶת־קַרְנ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֗ם הַנֹּשְׂאִ֥ים קֶ֛רֶן אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָ֖ה לְזָרוֹתָֽהּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I said, What [are] these coming to do? And he said, saying, These [are] the horns which scattered Judah, according to [the] mouth of [a] man not he lifted his head; and have come these to terrify them, to cast down [the] horns of the nations who lift a horn against [the] land of Judah to scatter it.

en.L: And I said, "What are these coming to do?" And he said, "These [are] the horns that scattered Judah, so that no one lifted up {{gender:their|his}} head; and these have come to terrify them, to throw down the horns of the nations that lifted up a horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."
en.B: I asked, "What are these coming to do?" He said, "Those are the horns that scattered Judah so completely that no one could raise {{gender:their|his}} head. But these craftsmen have come to terrify them, to throw down the horns of the nations that raised their horns against the land of Judah to scatter its people."
en.R: I asked, "What are these workers coming to do?" He said, "Those horns scattered the people of Judah so badly that no one could even lift {{gender:their|his}} head. These workers have come to terrify them and knock down the horns of the nations. Those nations raised their horns against the land of Judah to scatter its people."

es.L: Y dije: «¿Qué vienen a hacer estos?». Y él dijo: «Estos [son] los cuernos que dispersaron a Judá, de modo que nadie levantó la cabeza; y estos han venido para aterrorizarlos, para derribar los cuernos de las naciones que alzaron el cuerno contra la tierra de Judá para dispersarla».
es.B: Pregunté: «¿Qué vienen a hacer estos?». Él dijo: «Aquellos son los cuernos que dispersaron a Judá de tal manera que nadie podía levantar la cabeza. Pero estos artesanos han venido para aterrorizarlos, para derribar los cuernos de las naciones que alzaron sus cuernos contra la tierra de Judá para dispersar a su pueblo».
es.R: Pregunté: «¿Qué vienen a hacer estos obreros?». Él me dijo: «Esos cuernos dispersaron a la gente de Judá tanto que nadie podía siquiera levantar la cabeza. Estos obreros han venido a aterrorizarlos y a derribar los cuernos de las naciones. Esas naciones alzaron sus cuernos contra la tierra de Judá para dispersar a su pueblo».

fr.L: Et je dis : « Que viennent faire ceux-ci ? » Et il dit : « Ce [sont] les cornes qui ont dispersé Juda, au point que personne n’a relevé la tête ; et ceux-ci sont venus pour les terrifier, pour abattre les cornes des nations qui ont levé la corne contre le pays de Juda pour le disperser. »
fr.B: Je demandai : « Que viennent faire ceux-ci ? » Il dit : « Celles-là sont les cornes qui ont dispersé Juda, si bien que personne ne pouvait relever la tête. Mais ces artisans sont venus pour les terrifier, pour abattre les cornes des nations qui ont levé leurs cornes contre le pays de Juda afin d’en disperser le peuple. »
fr.R: J’ai demandé : « Que viennent faire ces ouvriers ? » Il a dit : « Ces cornes ont dispersé le peuple de Juda si durement que personne ne pouvait même plus relever la tête. Ces ouvriers sont venus pour les terrifier et abattre les cornes des nations. Ces nations ont levé leurs cornes contre le pays de Juda pour en disperser le peuple. »

sw.L: Nikasema, "Hawa wanakuja kufanya nini?" Naye akasema, "Hizi [ndizo] pembe zilizomtawanya Yuda, hata hakuna mtu aliyeinua kichwa chake; na hawa wamekuja kuzitia hofu, kuziangusha pembe za mataifa yaliyoinua pembe dhidi ya nchi ya Yuda ili kuitawanya."
sw.B: Nikauliza, "Hawa wanakuja kufanya nini?" Akasema, "Zile ni pembe zilizomtawanya Yuda kabisa hata hakuna mtu aliyeweza kuinua kichwa chake. Lakini mafundi hawa wamekuja kuzitia hofu, kuziangusha pembe za mataifa yaliyoinua pembe zao dhidi ya nchi ya Yuda ili kuwatawanya watu wake."
sw.R: Nikauliza, "Mafundi hawa wanakuja kufanya nini?" Akasema, "Zile pembe ziliwatawanya watu wa Yuda vibaya sana hata hakuna mtu aliyeweza kuinua kichwa chake. Mafundi hawa wamekuja kuzitia hofu na kuziangusha pembe za mataifa. Mataifa hayo yaliinua pembe zao dhidi ya nchi ya Yuda ili kuwatawanya watu wake."

vi.L: Tôi nói: "Những người này đến để làm gì?" Và người nói rằng: "Đây [là] những cái sừng đã làm tan lạc Giu-đa, đến nỗi không ai ngóc đầu lên được; và những người này đã đến để làm cho chúng kinh hãi, để quăng xuống những cái sừng của các nước đã giơ sừng lên chống lại đất Giu-đa để làm tan lạc nó."
vi.B: Tôi hỏi: "Những người này đến để làm gì?" Thiên sứ đáp: "Đó là những cái sừng đã làm tan lạc Giu-đa đến nỗi không ai ngẩng đầu lên được. Nhưng những người thợ này đã đến để làm cho chúng khiếp sợ, để quật ngã sừng của các nước đã giơ sừng lên chống lại đất Giu-đa và làm cho dân xứ ấy tan lạc."
vi.R: Tôi hỏi: "Những người thợ này đến để làm gì?" Thiên sứ bảo: "Những cái sừng kia đã làm cho dân Giu-đa tan lạc thảm hại đến nỗi không ai còn ngẩng đầu lên được. Những người thợ này đến để làm cho chúng khiếp sợ và quật ngã sừng của các nước. Các nước ấy đã giơ sừng lên chống lại đất Giu-đa để làm cho dân xứ ấy tan lạc."

ko.L: 그래서 내가 말하였다. "이들은 무엇을 하러 옵니까?" 그러자 그가 말하였다. "이것들은 유다를 흩어 버려 아무도 머리를 들지 못하게 한 뿔들이다. 이들은 그것들을 두렵게 하고, 유다 땅을 향해 뿔을 들어 그 땅을 흩어 버린 민족들의 뿔을 떨어뜨리려고 왔다."
ko.B: 내가 물었다. "이들은 무엇을 하러 옵니까?" 그가 말했다. "저것들은 유다를 흩어 버려서 아무도 고개를 들 수 없게 한 뿔들이다. 그러나 이 장인들은 그 뿔들을 두렵게 하고, 유다 땅을 향해 뿔을 들어 그 백성을 흩어 버린 민족들의 뿔을 꺾어 버리려고 왔다."
ko.R: 내가 물었다. "이 기술자들은 무엇을 하러 옵니까?" 그가 말했다. "저 뿔들이 유다 백성을 몹시 흩어 버려서 아무도 고개조차 들 수 없었다. 이 기술자들은 그 뿔들을 두렵게 하고, 민족들의 뿔을 꺾으려고 왔다. 그 민족들은 유다 땅을 향해 뿔을 들고 그 백성을 흩어 버렸다."

decisions.choice: so that no one lifted up his head: so completely that everyone was crushed and humbled
decisions.reason: "According to the mouth of a man" means "in proportion to", here "to such a degree that". Not lifting the head is a picture of defeat and shame (Judges 8:28; Job 10:15). The scattering left no one able to stand up straight.

decisions.choice: lifted up a horn against: rose up in proud strength against
decisions.reason: To lift up the horn is to act with power, often with arrogance (Psalm 75:5-6). The nations that raised their horns against Judah will have their horns thrown down.

decisions.choice: to throw down: to cast down and destroy the horns
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to throw or cast (Lamentations 3:53, of stones). Here it is used of horns, so it may mean to knock them down or cut them off. Either way the power of the nations is broken.

decisions.choice: to terrify them: the craftsmen frighten the horns, that is, the nations they stand for
decisions.reason: The word "them" has no clear reference in the Hebrew. It most likely points to the horns or the nations behind them. The angel does not say who the craftsmen are; the vision says only that God has agents ready to break every power that harmed his people.

decisions.choice: these craftsmen (B); these workers (R); its people (B, R); the gender setting
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "these", and the reader needs to know that the craftsmen are meant. "Scatter it" means scattering the land's people, as Balanced and Readable say. "No one lifted his head" means men and women alike, so the pronoun takes the gender setting. Readable splits the long explanation into sentences but keeps the horns.

decisions.choice: "nadie levantó la cabeza", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Where the English needs a gender setting for "his head", Spanish says "la cabeza" with no possessive, which already covers men and women.

decisions.choice: "personne n'a relevé la tête", with no gender span
decisions.reason: French says "la tête" without a possessive, so the English gender setting has nothing to attach to.

decisions.choice: "hakuna mtu aliyeinua kichwa chake", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Chake" covers both sexes, so Swahili needs no gender setting where the English has one.

decisions.choice: "không ai ngóc đầu lên được", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Không ai" already covers men and women, so the English gender setting is not needed.

decisions.choice: "아무도 머리를 들지 못하게", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean needs no pronoun here, so the English gender setting is not needed.

source.text: וָאֶשָּׂ֥א עֵינַ֛י וָאֵ֖רֶא וְהִנֵּה־אִ֑ישׁ וּבְיָד֖וֹ חֶ֥בֶל מִדָּֽה׃

decisions.choice: This verse is 2:5 in the Hebrew text, 2:1 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: Bibles that number Hebrew 2:1-4 as 1:18-21 begin their chapter 2 here, so Hebrew 2:5-17 is their 2:1-13. See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: the third vision: a man with a measuring line, and a city too full for walls
decisions.reason: The man sets out to measure Jerusalem (verse 6), but another angel brings word that the city will spread beyond any wall, because the LORD himself will be its wall and its glory (verses 8-9). The vision takes up the promise of 1:16, that a line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a measuring line: a cord used to measure land and buildings
decisions.reason: The word is a different one from the "line" of 1:16, a length of cord or rope used for measuring (Amos 7:17; Psalm 78:55). Ezekiel also saw a man with a measuring line who measured the temple to come (Ezekiel 40:3).

decisions.choice: there was (B); not shown (R)

decisions.choice: one angel tells the other to run to Zechariah, the young man
alternatives: the young man is the man with the measuring line
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he said to him". Most likely the second angel sends the angel who talked with Zechariah back to him with the message. "This young man" is most likely Zechariah himself, who must pass the word on; some take him to be the man with the measuring line, who needs to know that Jerusalem cannot be measured. The message is the same either way.

decisions.choice: open villages: settlements without walls
decisions.reason: The word means open country towns with no walls (Ezekiel 38:11; Esther 9:19). Jerusalem will be like them, not because it is weak but because it will be too full of people and flocks for any wall to hold.

decisions.choice: people and livestock: a city full of life and wealth
decisions.reason: Flocks and herds were a family's wealth. A city with many people and animals is a prosperous one. In Zechariah's day, Jerusalem had few people and its walls were in ruins (compare Nehemiah 1:3; 7:4).

decisions.choice: that young man (B, R); like villages without walls (B); like a village with no walls around it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "that young man", since the speaker is pointing to someone else. They add "like", to make plain that Jerusalem will be like open villages, not turned into them. The message to be passed on is in single quotation marks and closes at the end of verse 9.

decisions.choice: "aldeas abiertas" (L), "aldeas sin muros" (B), "una aldea sin muros a su alrededor" (R)
decisions.reason: The word names open country villages with no walls (m2). The angel's words open with « and the message inside them with “; both close at the end of verse 9.

decisions.choice: "des villages ouverts" (L), "des villages sans murailles" (B), "un village sans murailles" (R)
decisions.reason: Open villages are settlements without walls (m2). The outer « » and inner “ ” open here and close at the end of verse 9, as the English marks.

decisions.choice: "성벽 없는 마을들"
decisions.reason: The open villages are towns with no walls (m2). The angel's words take " " and the message inside them ' ', closing at the end of verse 9.

decisions.choice: a wall of fire all around: the LORD himself will protect the city
decisions.reason: The city does not need walls of stone, for the LORD will surround it. The fire recalls the pillar of fire that guarded Israel in the wilderness (Exodus 13:21-22; 14:24) and Isaiah's promise of a glow of fire over Zion (Isaiah 4:5).

decisions.choice: I will be the glory in her midst: the LORD's own presence will return to the city
decisions.reason: Ezekiel saw the glory of the LORD leave the temple and the city before the fall of Jerusalem (Ezekiel 10:18-19; 11:23), and later saw it come back (Ezekiel 43:2-5). Haggai promised that the LORD would fill the new temple with glory (Haggai 2:7, 9). The LORD will not only guard the city from outside; he will live in it.

decisions.choice: I myself: the LORD stresses that he will do it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with the pronoun "I", which it does not need, to stress who will be the city's wall.

decisions.choice: around the city (R); its glory there inside it (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the city for "her", and makes "for glory" plain as "its glory". The closing marks end the message and the angel's words.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다" placed at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The formula stands as its own sentence in Korean, so it follows the promise instead of interrupting it as it does in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: 2:10-17: a poem that calls the exiles home and promises the LORD's coming
decisions.reason: After the vision, the prophet speaks in verse: a call to the exiles still in Babylon to flee (verses 10-11), a word against the nations (verses 12-13) and a call to Zion to rejoice because the LORD is coming to live among his people (verses 14-17). The prophet speaks the LORD's words and, in verses 12-15, also of his own sending. As in the other prophets, the poem takes no quotation marks. It is set in lines.

decisions.choice: Ho! Ho!: an urgent call to listen and act
decisions.reason: The word is most often a cry of woe over those facing judgment (Isaiah 5:8), but it is also used to call out to people, as in Isaiah 55:1 ("Ho, everyone who thirsts"). Here it is doubled and followed by "flee", so it is a summons to hurry, not a threat.

decisions.choice: the land of the north: Babylon
decisions.reason: Verse 11 names Babylon. It lay to the east, but armies and travelers from there came into Judah from the north, so the prophets speak of the enemy as coming from the north (Jeremiah 1:14; 6:22). After Cyrus allowed the Jews to return in 538 BC, many stayed in Babylon; the poem calls them to come home.

decisions.choice: like the four winds I have spread you: I scattered you in every direction
alternatives: I will spread you out as widely as the four winds
I will gather you from the four winds
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act and usually means to spread out. Read with "flee", it looks back on the exile, when the LORD scattered his people to every quarter, as the wind blows in all directions (Ezekiel 17:21). Some read it as a promise that the LORD will make his people spread out widely in the future. The Greek translation reads "I will gather you from the four winds of heaven", which is a different sense and probably a smoothing of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Ho! Ho! (L); Come! Come! (B); Hurry! Hurry! (R); no quotation marks; set in lines
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "Ho", as Isaiah 55:1 does for the same call. Balanced and Readable use a word that a reader hears as a summons, since this is not a cry of woe (m2). The lines follow the main division of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "¡Eh, eh!" (L), "¡Vengan! ¡Vengan!" with plural_you (B), "¡Rápido! ¡Rápido!" (R)
decisions.reason: The cry here is a summons, not a woe (m2), so Spanish uses the term sheet's words for "hoy" as a call. The exiles are a group, so the imperatives and "los/os" take plural_you. The poem takes no quotation marks and keeps the English lines.

decisions.choice: "Ho ! Ho !" (L), "Venez ! Venez !" (B), "Vite ! Vite !" (R)
decisions.reason: The summons of the term sheet for "hoy" in Zechariah 2:10-11; it calls the exiles home and is not a woe (m2). The poem is speech (present and passé composé) and takes no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "Haya! Haya!" (L), "Njooni! Njooni!" (B), "Harakisheni! Harakisheni!" (R)
decisions.reason: "Hoy" is a call here, not a cry of woe (m2), so Swahili uses words of summons, not the "Ole" of the woe oracles. The poem takes no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "Này! Này!" (L), "Hãy đến! Hãy đến!" (B), "Mau lên! Mau lên!" (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a summons here (m2), so Vietnamese does not use "Khốn cho", which is kept for woe. The exiles are "các ngươi" at every level.

decisions.choice: "자, 자!" (L), "어서, 어서!" (B), "어서, 서둘러라!" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's words for "hoy" as a summons (Zechariah 2:10-11), kept apart from the woe formula. The poem takes no quotation marks; the "declares" formulas stand as their own sentences.

decisions.choice: Zion: the exiles of Jerusalem still living in Babylon
decisions.reason: Zion is the hill of Jerusalem and so the city and its people. Here it is the part of the people still in exile, called to escape as Isaiah and Jeremiah had called them (Isaiah 48:20; Jeremiah 51:6, 45).

decisions.choice: daughter of Babylon: Babylon pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: Cities are often pictured as women (Isaiah 47:1; Psalm 137:8). "Daughter of Babylon" means Babylon itself, not a daughter of it.

decisions.choice: "la hija de Babilonia" (L, B), "Babilonia" (R); "tú" to Zion

decisions.choice: "Njooni, watu wa Sayuni! ... Okokeni, ninyi mnaoishi Babeli!"
decisions.reason: Readable says "people of Zion", as the English Readable does, so the call becomes plural; Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's singular address to Zion.

vi.L: Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này, sau vinh quang {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã sai tôi đến các nước đã cướp bóc các ngươi: \q vì kẻ nào đụng đến các ngươi là đụng đến con ngươi của mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán. Vì vinh quang của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã sai tôi đi nghịch cùng các nước đã cướp đoạt các ngươi. \q Ai đụng đến các ngươi là đụng đến con ngươi của mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 참으로 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 영광 뒤에 그분께서 너희를 약탈한 민족들에게 나를 보내셨다. \q 너희를 건드리는 자는 그분의 눈동자를 건드리는 것이다.
ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 그분께서 그분의 영광을 위하여 너희를 약탈한 민족들에게 나를 보내셨다. \q 너희를 건드리는 자는 그분의 눈동자를 건드리는 것이다.
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 그분께서 자신의 영광을 위하여 너희 것을 빼앗은 민족들에게 나를 보내셨다. \q 누구든지 너희를 건드리면 그분의 눈동자를 건드리는 것이다.

decisions.choice: after glory: for the sake of the LORD's glory
alternatives: after the glory appeared, he sent me
decisions.reason: These two words are among the hardest in the book. "After" can mean "behind" or "for the sake of", and "glory" can mean God's glory or honor in general. Read one way, the LORD sent the speaker to the nations for his glory: to win honor for the LORD by bringing judgment. Read another way, the speaker was sent after the glory had been revealed, perhaps the glory promised in verse 9. The translation takes the first; the sense of the verse, that the LORD will act against the nations, is the same.

decisions.choice: sent me: the prophet, sent with this message
alternatives: a figure sent by the LORD
decisions.reason: The speaker says that the LORD of hosts has sent him, and three times adds that when the promise comes true, "you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me" (verses 13, 15; 4:9; 6:15). This is the test of a true prophet (Deuteronomy 18:21-22), so the speaker is most likely Zechariah. Some read him as the angel, or as a messenger of the LORD whom later readers saw as the Messiah.

decisions.choice: the pupil of his eye: what is most precious and most easily hurt
decisions.reason: The eye is guarded by instinct against the smallest touch. To touch God's people is to strike at what God holds most dear and guards most closely (Deuteronomy 32:10; Psalm 17:8).

decisions.choice: his eye: the LORD's eye
decisions.reason: The word for pupil is found only here. Jewish scribal tradition lists this verse among a few places where the scribes changed "my" to "his" out of reverence, so that the text would not speak of touching God's own eye; the original then said "my eye". The Hebrew as it stands can also be read of the attacker's own eye: whoever harms Israel harms himself. The translation reads it of the LORD, as Deuteronomy 32:10 does. This description of the scribal tradition is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: the pupil of his eye (all levels); after glory (L); for the sake of his glory (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Pupil of his eye" is the wording of Deuteronomy 32:10 at each level. "Apple of the eye", an old English idiom, now means a favorite, which is weaker than the picture. Literal keeps "after glory" and leaves its sense open; Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in m1. "Plundered" (L, B) becomes "robbed" at Readable.

decisions.choice: "la pupila de su ojo" (L), "la niña de sus ojos" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording of the published Deuteronomy 32:10 at each level, the passage this picture comes from; "los/os" with plural_you, since the Hebrew "you" is plural.

decisions.choice: "la pupille de son œil" (L), "la prunelle de son œil" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Deuteronomy 32:10 at each level. The speaker who is sent is the prophet, who speaks of the LORD in the third person, so "il" and "son" take the pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "mboni ya jicho lake"
decisions.reason: As Deuteronomy 32:10. The pronoun setting goes on the free possessives "wake" and "lake", never on the verb.

decisions.choice: "con ngươi của mắt Ngài"
decisions.reason: As Deuteronomy 32:10 L. The prophet speaks of the LORD as "Ngài" and of himself as "tôi".

decisions.choice: "그분께서 ... 나를 보내셨다"; "그분의 눈동자"
decisions.reason: The prophet, the one sent, speaks about God, so God takes the honorific and 그분, and "the pupil of his eye" follows Deuteronomy 32:10 (그분의 눈동자).

source.text: כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֨י מֵנִ֤יף אֶת־יָדִי֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔םוְהָי֥וּ שָׁלָ֖ל לְעַבְדֵיהֶ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחָֽנִי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For look, I [am] about to wave my hand over them, and they will be plunder for their slaves; and you will know that Yahweh of hosts has sent me.

en.L: For look, I am about to wave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand over them, and they will be plunder for their own slaves; \q and you shall know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has sent me.
en.B: I am about to raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against them, and they will be plundered by their own slaves. \q Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me.
en.R: I am going to raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to strike them, and they will be robbed by the people they made their slaves. \q Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me.

es.L: Porque he aquí, yo agito {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano sobre ellas, y serán botín para sus propios esclavos; \q y {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos me ha enviado.
es.B: Voy a levantar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano contra ellas, y serán saqueadas por sus propios esclavos. \q Entonces {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos me ha enviado.
es.R: Voy a levantar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano para golpearlas, y las robarán aquellos a quienes ellas hicieron esclavos. \q Entonces {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos me ha enviado.

fr.L: Car voici, j’agite {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main sur elles, et elles deviendront le butin de leurs propres esclaves ; \q et vous saurez que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé.
fr.B: Je vais lever {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main contre elles, et elles seront pillées par leurs propres esclaves. \q Alors vous saurez que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé.
fr.R: Je vais lever {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main pour les frapper, et elles seront dépouillées par ceux dont elles avaient fait leurs esclaves. \q Alors vous saurez que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé.

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, ninakaribia kuutikisa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} juu yao, nao watakuwa mateka kwa watumwa wao wenyewe; \q nanyi mtajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma.
sw.B: Nitainua mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} dhidi yao, nao watatekwa nyara na watumwa wao wenyewe. \q Ndipo mtakapojua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma.
sw.R: Nitainua mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kuwapiga, nao watanyang'anywa mali zao na wale waliowafanya watumwa. \q Ndipo mtakapojua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma.

vi.L: Vì kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp vung tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trên chúng, và chúng sẽ thành của cướp cho chính những kẻ nô lệ của chúng; \q và các ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi.
vi.B: Ta sắp giơ tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lên chống lại chúng, và chúng sẽ bị chính những nô lệ của mình cướp bóc. \q Bấy giờ các ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi.
vi.R: Ta sắp giơ tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lên đánh chúng, và chúng sẽ bị chính những người chúng bắt làm nô lệ cướp đoạt. \q Khi ấy các ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi.

ko.L: 보라, 내가 그들 위로 내 손을 휘두르겠다. 그러면 그들이 자기들의 노예들에게 약탈물이 될 것이다. \q 그때에 너희는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 그들을 치려고 손을 들겠다. 그러면 그들이 자기들의 노예들에게 약탈당할 것이다. \q 그때에 너희는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 손을 들어 그들을 치겠다. 그러면 그들이 노예로 부리던 사람들에게 빼앗길 것이다. \q 그때에 너희는 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: wave my hand over them: raise the hand to strike
decisions.reason: To wave or shake the hand over someone is a threatening gesture before a blow (Isaiah 11:15; 19:16). Here the LORD is the one who raises his hand against the nations.

decisions.choice: my hand ... sent me: the LORD speaks, and then his messenger
decisions.reason: "My hand" is the LORD's, but "the LORD of hosts has sent me" is said by the messenger. The prophet passes from speaking the LORD's words to speaking about his own task without a break, as prophets often do.

decisions.choice: plunder for their own slaves: the nations' power will be turned upside down
decisions.reason: The nations that plundered God's people (verse 12) will be plundered by those they had made their slaves. The reversal is like Isaiah 14:2.

decisions.choice: slaves, at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "slave" at every level where slavery itself is the point. Here the masters are plundered by the people they had enslaved, and "servants" would hide the reversal.

decisions.choice: "esclavos"; "{{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que ... me ha enviado"
decisions.reason: Slavery itself is the point (the masters plundered by those they enslaved), so Spanish says "esclavos", as the English says "slaves". The hearers are plural, and "me" in the last line is the messenger, so it takes no pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 보내신 줄"; "노예들"
decisions.reason: The last line is the messenger speaking about God, so God takes the honorific, while "my hand" in the first line is God's own word with none. 노예 is used because slavery itself is meant; 종 stays for God's servants.

source.text: רָנִּ֥י וְשִׂמְחִ֖י בַּת־צִיּ֑וֹן כִּ֧י הִנְנִי־בָ֛א וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for look, I [am] coming and I will dwell in your midst, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: Shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion, \q for look, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Sing and rejoice, Daughter Zion, \q for I am coming to live among you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: People of Zion, sing and be glad! \q I am coming, and I will live among you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Grita de júbilo y alégrate, hija de Sion, \q porque he aquí, yo vengo, y habitaré en medio de ti, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Lanza gritos de alegría y regocíjate, hija de Sion, \q porque vengo a vivir en medio de ti, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: ¡Pueblo de Sion, canta con alegría! \q Ya vengo, y viviré en medio de ti, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Crie de joie et réjouis-toi, fille de Sion, \q car voici, je viens et je demeurerai au milieu de toi, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Chante et sois dans la joie, fille de Sion, \q car je viens habiter parmi toi, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Peuple de Sion, chante et sois heureux ! \q Je viens, et je vivrai au milieu de toi, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Imba kwa furaha na ushangilie, binti Sayuni, \q kwa maana tazama, ninakuja, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakaa katikati yako, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Imba na ufurahi, Binti Sayuni, \q kwa maana ninakuja kukaa kati yako, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Sayuni, imbeni na mfurahi! \q Ninakuja, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitaishi kati yenu, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Hãy reo hò và vui mừng, hỡi con gái Si-ôn, \q vì kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ngự giữa ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Hãy ca hát và vui mừng, hỡi con gái Si-ôn, \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến để ngự giữa con, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Hỡi dân Si-ôn, hãy ca hát và vui mừng! \q Ta đang đến, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sống giữa các con, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 딸 시온아, 기뻐 외치며 즐거워하여라. \q 보라, 내가 가서 네 가운데 머물겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 딸 시온아, 노래하며 기뻐하여라. \q 내가 너에게 가서 네 가운데 살겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 시온 백성아, 노래하며 기뻐하여라! \q 내가 가서 너희 가운데 살겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: I am coming and I will dwell in your midst: the LORD's own presence among his people
decisions.reason: The verb "dwell" is the one used for the LORD's living among Israel in the tabernacle (Exodus 25:8; 29:45-46). Ezekiel had promised that he would live among his people forever (Ezekiel 43:7, 9). The promise returns in 8:3.

decisions.choice: shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion
decisions.reason: Zephaniah 3:14-15 calls Zion to sing and rejoice because the LORD is in her midst, and Zechariah 9:9 repeats the call when Zion's king comes. On "daughter of Zion", see the note at Isaiah 1:8.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion (L); Daughter Zion (B); people of Zion (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording from Isaiah. Balanced and Readable leave out "look", and Readable says "live among you" for "dwell in your midst".

decisions.choice: "hija de Sion" (L, B), "pueblo de Sion" (R); "habitaré en medio de ti" (L)
decisions.reason: The daughter-Zion wording of the Spanish prophets; Zion is "tú". The line is drafted from the Hebrew and kept apart from familiar older wordings of this verse.

decisions.choice: "fille de Sion" (L, B), "peuple de Sion" (R); "je demeurerai au milieu de toi" (L), "habiter parmi toi" (B)
decisions.reason: The daughter-Zion wording of the French prophets, with Zion as "tu"; the lines are drafted from the Hebrew, not from a familiar version.

decisions.choice: God says "con" (B) / "các con" (R) to Zion; "ngươi" (L)
decisions.reason: In the tender promises God speaks to Zion with "con" at Balanced and Readable, as the term sheet sets for such passages; Readable addresses the "people of Zion", so the plural "các con".

source.text: וְנִלְווּ֩ גוֹיִ֨ם רַבִּ֤ים אֶל־יְהוָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֣י בְתוֹכֵ֔ךְ וְיָדַ֕עַתְּ כִּי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֵלָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will join themselves many nations to Yahweh in that day, and they will become for me a people; and I will dwell in your midst, and you will know that Yahweh of hosts has sent me to you.

en.L: And many nations will join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in that day, and they will be a people for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q and I will dwell in your midst, and you shall know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has sent me to you.
en.B: Many nations will join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on that day and will become {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q I will live among you, and you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you.
en.R: At that time many nations will join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and become {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q I will live among you. Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you.

es.L: Y muchas naciones se unirán {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} en aquel día, y serán para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} un pueblo; \q y habitaré en medio de ti, y sabrás que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos me ha enviado a ti.
es.B: Muchas naciones se unirán {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} aquel día y llegarán a ser {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo. \q Viviré en medio de ti, y sabrás que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos me ha enviado a ti.
es.R: En ese tiempo muchas naciones se unirán {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y serán {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo. \q Viviré en medio de ti. Entonces sabrás que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos me ha enviado a ti.

fr.L: Et des nations nombreuses s’attacheront {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} en ce jour-là, et elles seront pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} un peuple ; \q et j’habiterai au milieu de toi, et tu sauras que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé vers toi.
fr.B: Beaucoup de nations s’attacheront {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ce jour-là et deviendront {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple. \q J’habiterai parmi toi, et tu sauras que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé vers toi.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, beaucoup de nations s’attacheront {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et deviendront {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple. \q Je vivrai au milieu de toi. Alors tu sauras que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé vers toi.

sw.L: Na mataifa mengi yatajiunga na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika siku ile, nao watakuwa watu kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakaa katikati yako, nawe utajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwako.
sw.B: Mataifa mengi yatajiunga na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} siku hiyo na kuwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Nitakaa kati yako, nawe utajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwako.
sw.R: Wakati huo mataifa mengi yatajiunga na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kuwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Nitaishi kati yako. Ndipo utakapojua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwako.

vi.L: Và trong ngày ấy, nhiều nước sẽ liên kết với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và họ sẽ trở nên dân của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ngự giữa ngươi, và ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến với ngươi.
vi.B: Vào ngày ấy, nhiều nước sẽ gắn bó với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và trở thành dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Ta sẽ ngự giữa con, và con sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến với con.
vi.R: Vào lúc ấy, nhiều nước sẽ gắn bó với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và trở thành dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Ta sẽ sống giữa con. Khi ấy con sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến với con.

ko.L: 그날에 많은 민족들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게 연합하여 나의 백성이 될 것이다. \q 내가 네 가운데 머물 것이니, 너는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.
ko.B: 그날에 많은 민족들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게 와서 연합하여 내 백성이 될 것이다. \q 나는 네 가운데 살 것이다. 그러면 너는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 그때에 많은 민족들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게 와서 내 백성이 될 것이다. \q 나는 네 가운데 살 것이다. 그때에 너는 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: many nations will join themselves to the LORD and become his people
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of foreigners who "join themselves to the LORD" in Isaiah 56:3, 6. The words "they will be my people" are the words of God's covenant with Israel (Jeremiah 31:33; Zechariah 8:8); here they include the nations. The same hope closes the book's first half (8:20-23).

decisions.choice: for me ... has sent me: the LORD speaks, then the messenger
decisions.reason: As in verse 13, "me" first refers to the LORD and then to the one he has sent. "You" is feminine singular: Zion is addressed.

decisions.choice: in that day (L); on that day (B); at that time (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase in the prophets.

decisions.choice: "en aquel día" (L), "aquel día" (B), "en ese tiempo" (R); "sabrás", singular
decisions.reason: The prophets' wording for "in that day". The "you" of this verse is feminine singular, Zion (m2), so Spanish uses tú and no plural_you.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게 연합하여 나의 백성이 될 것이다"
decisions.reason: The first half is God's own word, so the name takes the plain particle 에게 rather than the honorific 께; the last line, about the one sent, gives God the honorific.

source.text: וְנָחַ֨ל יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יְהוּדָה֙ חֶלְק֔וֹ עַ֖ל אַדְמַ֣ת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וּבָחַ֥ר ע֖וֹד בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will inherit Yahweh Judah [as] his portion on the land the holy, and he will choose again Jerusalem.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will inherit Judah [as] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} portion upon the holy land, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will again choose Jerusalem.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will possess Judah as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} share in the holy land, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will once again choose Jerusalem.
en.R: Judah will belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own share in the holy land. \q He will choose Jerusalem again.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} heredará a Judá [como] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} porción en la tierra santa, \q y escogerá otra vez a Jerusalén.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} poseerá a Judá como {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} parte en la tierra santa, \q y una vez más escogerá a Jerusalén.
es.R: Judá pertenecerá {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} como {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia parte en la tierra santa. \q Él escogerá de nuevo a Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} héritera de Juda [comme] {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} part sur la terre sainte, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} choisira encore Jérusalem.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} prendra possession de Juda comme de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} part dans la terre sainte, \q et une fois de plus {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} choisira Jérusalem.
fr.R: Juda appartiendra {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : ce sera {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} part à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dans la terre sainte. \q Il choisira de nouveau Jérusalem.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamrithi Yuda [kuwa] fungu {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} katika nchi takatifu, \q naye ataichagua tena Yerusalemu.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamiliki Yuda kama sehemu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} katika nchi takatifu, \q naye ataichagua tena Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Yuda itakuwa mali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, sehemu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe katika nchi takatifu. \q Ataichagua Yerusalemu tena.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ nhận Giu-đa [làm] phần sản nghiệp của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên đất thánh, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ lại chọn Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ chiếm hữu Giu-đa làm phần của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong đất thánh, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ một lần nữa chọn Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Giu-đa sẽ thuộc về {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, làm phần riêng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong đất thánh. \q Ngài sẽ lại chọn Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 거룩한 땅에서 유다를 그분의 몫으로 [삼아] 상속하시고, \q 다시 예루살렘을 택하실 것이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 거룩한 땅에서 유다를 그분의 몫으로 차지하시고, \q 다시 한 번 예루살렘을 택하실 것이다.
ko.R: 유다는 거룩한 땅에서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 몫이 될 것이다. \q 그분께서 예루살렘을 다시 택하실 것이다.

decisions.choice: inherit Judah as his portion: claim Judah as his own share
decisions.reason: The verb means to receive or hold as one's inheritance. Deuteronomy 32:9 says, "The LORD's portion is his people". Here the LORD claims Judah again as his own.

decisions.choice: the holy land: the land made holy by the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: This is the only place in the Bible where the land is called "the holy land". It is holy because the LORD will live there (verses 14-15).

decisions.choice: he will again choose Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The promise of 1:17 repeated; see the note there.

decisions.choice: Judah will belong to the LORD (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes Judah the subject, which says the same thing in plainer words.

decisions.choice: "la tierra santa"
decisions.reason: The only place where the land is called "the holy land" (m2); Spanish keeps the plain words at every level, lowercase.

source.text: הַ֥ס כָּל־בָּשָׂ֖ר מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֥י נֵע֖וֹר מִמְּע֥וֹן קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Hush, all flesh, before Yahweh, for he has roused himself from [the] dwelling of his holiness.

en.L: Hush, all flesh, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has roused {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy dwelling.
en.B: Be silent before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all people, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has risen up from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy dwelling.
en.R: Everyone, be silent before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q He has gotten up and come out from the holy place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives.

es.L: Silencio, toda carne, ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se ha despertado desde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} morada santa.
es.B: Que toda la humanidad guarde silencio ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se ha levantado de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} morada santa.
es.R: ¡Que todos guarden silencio ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}! \q Él se ha levantado y ha salido del lugar santo donde {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} vive.

fr.L: Silence, toute chair, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est levé de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainte demeure.
fr.B: Faites silence devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, vous tous les humains, \q car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se lève et sort de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainte demeure.
fr.R: Que tout le monde se taise devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! \q Il s’est levé, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sort du lieu saint où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} habite.

sw.L: Kimya, kila mwenye mwili, mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q kwa maana amejiinua kutoka katika makao {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} matakatifu.
sw.B: Nyamazeni mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, watu wote, \q kwa maana ameinuka kutoka katika makao {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} matakatifu.
sw.R: Kila mtu na anyamaze mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Ameamka na kutoka mahali patakatifu anapoishi.

vi.L: Hỡi mọi xác thịt, hãy im lặng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã thức dậy từ nơi ngự thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Hỡi mọi người, hãy im lặng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đứng dậy từ nơi ngự thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Mọi người hãy im lặng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! \q Ngài đã đứng dậy và ra khỏi nơi thánh, là nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngự.

ko.L: 모든 육체여, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 잠잠하여라. \q 그분께서 그분의 거룩한 처소에서 일어나셨다.
ko.B: 모든 사람아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 잠잠하여라. \q 그분께서 거룩한 처소에서 일어나셨다.
ko.R: 모두 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 조용히 하여라! \q 그분께서 일어나셔서, 그분이 계시는 거룩한 곳에서 나오셨다.

decisions.choice: be silent before the LORD: hushed awe before God who is about to act
decisions.reason: The same call is found in Habakkuk 2:20 and Zephaniah 1:7. Silence is the response of creatures when God comes to act.

decisions.choice: all flesh: all humankind
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for human beings in their weakness and mortality, as in Joel 3:1. Every person, in every nation, is to be still.

decisions.choice: he has roused himself from his holy dwelling: the LORD has risen to act
decisions.reason: The verb is used of waking up or stirring oneself to action (Psalm 44:24; Isaiah 51:9). The LORD's holy dwelling is heaven (Deuteronomy 26:15; Jeremiah 25:30). He is coming out to do what he has promised.

decisions.choice: all flesh (L); all people (B); everyone (R)
decisions.reason: As set for Joel 3:1, Literal keeps "all flesh", and the other levels say what it means. Readable says "gotten up and come out" for "roused himself", to make the picture plain.

decisions.choice: "toda carne" (L), "toda la humanidad" (B), "todos" (R)
decisions.reason: As Joel 3:1 is set: Literal keeps "all flesh", and the other levels say what it means (m2). The line is drafted from the Hebrew and kept apart from the familiar older wording.

decisions.choice: "kila mwenye mwili" (L), "watu wote" (B), "kila mtu" (R)
decisions.reason: As Joel 3:1 in Swahili: Literal keeps "flesh", the other levels say "all people". The line is drafted from the Hebrew, not from the Union Version.
